# Homelessness

## Homelessness in MA in 2024

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total number of infants and children 0-5 that are homeless in MA"

ma_homeless_total_2024 <- ed_totals_under_5 |>
  filter(STATENAME == "MASSACHUSETTS" & YEAR_END == 2024) |>
  select(HOMELESS_UNDER_5_GRADE_1) |>
  pull()

list(
  icon = "hash",
  color = "info",

)
```


## Temporal Visualizations

```{r}
#| fill: false

options(scipen = 999)
ed_totals_under_5 |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(ST == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           ST != "MA" ~ "Other States")) |>
  group_by(YEAR_END, is_ma) |>
  filter(!is.na(is_ma)) |>
  summarize(homeless_children = sum(HOMELESS_UNDER_5_GRADE_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_population = sum(POPULATION_UNDER_5, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(YEAR_END) |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           is_ma != "MA" ~ "USA"),
         homeless_children = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ homeless_children,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(homeless_children, na.rm = TRUE)),
         total_population = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ total_population,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(total_population)),
         ,
      percent_homeless = homeless_children / total_population * 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR_END, y = percent_homeless, col = is_ma, group = is_ma)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous() +
  scale_y_continuous() +
  scale_color_manual(values = hs_palette) +
  labs(x = "Year", 
       y = "% Homeless Children",
       col = "",
       title = paste("Homeless Population via Grade 1 Proxy, ",
                     min(ed_totals_under_5$YEAR_END), 
                     "-" , 
                     max(ed_totals_under_5$YEAR_END))) +
  theme_minimal()  +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(percent_homeless, 2)), 
            vjust = -0.25)

```

## Rankings

```{r}
#| fill: false
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "How Massachusetts ranks compared to other states in terms of percent of children enrolled in Head Start that are homeless "

percent_homeless_table <-
  combined_pir |>
  group_by(pir_year, State) |>
  summarize(total_child_enroll = sum(A.10.g, na.rm = TRUE), 
      total_homeless_enroll = sum(C.48, na.rm = TRUE),
      num_homeless_na = sum(is.na(C.48)),
      percent_homeless = round(total_homeless_enroll / total_child_enroll * 100, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_homeless)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(pir_year) |>
  mutate(state_rank = rank(-percent_homeless, ties.method = "min")) |>
  ungroup()

ma_state_rank <- percent_homeless_table |>
  filter(State == "MA" & pir_year == 2024) |>
  select(state_rank) |>
  pull()

list(
  icon = "award",
  color = "info",
  value = ma_state_rank
)
```

```{r}

percent_homeless_table |>
```

```{r}
#| fill: false

us_states <- states(cb = TRUE, 
                    resolution = "20m", 
                    progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  left_join(percent_homeless_table |>
              filter(pir_year == 2024), by = c("STUSPS" = "State")) |>
  st_transform(4326)

labels <- paste("<strong>", 
                us_states$NAME,
                "</strong><br>Rank:", 
                us_states$state_rank,
                "<br>% Homeless Enrolled:",
                us_states$percent_homeless) |>
  lapply(htmltools::HTML)

pal_bin_state_rank <- colorBin(palette="BuGn", 
                    domain = us_states$percent_homeless,
                    bins = 5)

homeless_hs_map <- leaflet(width = "100%") %>%
  setView(lat = 30, lng = -95, zoom = 3) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.NatGeoWorldMap) |> 
  addPolygons(data = us_states, 
              weight = 1,
              color = "black",
              fillColor = ~pal_bin_state_rank(percent_homeless),
              fillOpacity = 0.8, 
              label = labels) |>
  addLegend(data = us_states,
            title = "% Homeless Enrolled HS", 
            pal = pal_bin_state_rank, 
            values = ~percent_homeless)

homeless_hs_map
```

## Overview of Homeless Counts from Different Sources

Counting the number of homeless children from ages 0-5 in the United States poses significant challenges. Annual point-in-time counts of sheltered and unsheltered homeless populations tracked by the Department of Housing and Urban Development count all homeless children under the age of 18, without further age disaggregation. Point-in-time counts also exclude individuals temporarily sheltered with family members, in motels, or in other hidden places. Public school counts of childhood homelessness tend to be higher because the Department of Education adopts the much broader McKinney-Vento Act definition of homelessness. However, public schools are often the first institution to identify a child's living status, and there are very few students under the age of 5 enrolled in public schools systems. Any child ages 0-5 that receives services as a result of a McKinney-Vento Subgrant Program gets counted by the Department of Education, but since many homeless children do not receive these services, this too is a poor proxy for estimating the extent of early childhood homelessness. 

Given these limitations, SchoolHouse Connection has developed a method of calculating homelessness that determines the percentage of homeless children in Grade 1 in a given year and region, and then applying that percentage to the population of children from ages 0-5 in that same year and region. To the right we can see that the Grade 1 proxy method identifies at least 9 times as many homeless children as any other method of estimation. Even the Grade 1 proxy method is an underestimate as research has shown that even public schools struggle to identify homeless children. 

See: Shephard, D.D., Hall, C.C., & Lamberton, C. (2021). Increasing identification of homeless students: An experimental evaluation of increased communication incorporating behavioral insights, Educational Researcher, 50(4), 239–248. https://doi.org/10.3102/0013189X20981067

```{r}
#| fill: false

ed_totals_under_5 |>
  mutate(HOMELESS_3_5_655 = as.numeric(HOMELESS_3_5_655),
         HOMELESS_0_5_818 = as.numeric(HOMELESS_0_5_818)) |>
  select(STATENAME, 
         YEAR_END, 
         HOMELESS_UNDER_5_GRADE_1,
         HOMELESS_3_5_655, 
         HOMELESS_0_5_818, 
         TOTAL_HS_HOMELESS_ENROLL) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(HOMELESS_UNDER_5_GRADE_1, 
               HOMELESS_3_5_655, 
               HOMELESS_0_5_818, 
               TOTAL_HS_HOMELESS_ENROLL),
               names_to = "HOMELESS_MEASURE",
               values_to = "HOMELESS_COUNT") |>
  mutate(HOMELESS_MEASURE = case_when(HOMELESS_MEASURE == "HOMELESS_UNDER_5_GRADE_1" ~
                                        "Grade 1 Proxy Method",
                                      HOMELESS_MEASURE == "HOMELESS_3_5_655" ~
                                        "Chidren 3-5 Enrolled in Public Schools (File 655)",
                                      HOMELESS_MEASURE == "HOMELESS_0_5_818" ~
                                        "Children 0-5 Served by McKinney-Vento subgrant funds (File 818)",
                                      HOMELESS_MEASURE == "TOTAL_HS_HOMELESS_ENROLL" ~
                                        "Homeless Children Enrolled in Head Start")) |>
  filter(STATENAME == "MASSACHUSETTS") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR_END, 
             y = HOMELESS_COUNT, 
             col = HOMELESS_MEASURE, 
             group = HOMELESS_MEASURE)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = hs_palette) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 5))  +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = HOMELESS_COUNT), 
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Homeless Count", col = "Metric Used to Measure Homelessness")
  
```


## By Shelter Type

The NPRM’s elimination of self-attestation would be detrimental to Head Start’s promise to serve the homeless population population. According to Department of Education data, in 2024, 66.9% of K-12 homeless students in Massachusetts were not living in emergency or transitional shelters but instead doubled up, living in hotels or motels, or unsheltered. These children meet the McKinney-Vento Act definition of homelessness but do not have access to immediate documentation of their status. This percentage is the closest we can come to estimating shelter situations for infants and children ages 0 to 5 since many homeless children are not counted until they enrolled in public schools. When we apply this percentage to the population of infants and children 0 to 5 in Massachusetts, the proposed changes would leave an estimated 13,024 homeless children across the state without the means to secure documentation for their enrollment in Head Start.

For footnote: Shelter type is not reported disaggregated by grade. We took the percentage of K-12 students in each shelter type, each year for each state and multiplied that percentage by the number of homeless children under 5 identified via the Grade 1 proxy method.

# Disability

## IDEA Overview
IDEA, or the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, is the law that ensures all children have access to education regardless of disability. This means that children served by IDEA are those who require early intervention (e.g., speech or occupational therapy), special education, or another disability-related service.

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "How MA ranks against other states in terms of percent of children enrolled in Head Start receiving IDEA services"

  group_by(pir_year, State) |>

            total_child_enroll = sum(A.10.g, na.rm = TRUE),
      percent_disabled = round(disabled_children / total_child_enroll * 100, 2)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(pir_year) |>

  ungroup()

  filter(State == "MA" & pir_year == 2024) |>
  select(state_rank) |>
  pull()

  icon = "award",
  color = "info",
  value = ma_ranking
)
```

# Dual Language Educators

## Bilingual Teachers in MA in 2024
The NPRM prohibits preferential hiring for bilingual educators and promoting bilingualism at Head Start. It estimates that about 1 in 3 bilingual Head Start educators would lose their jobs as a result of this change, as it claims that not all bilingual educators could be retrained for English-only instruction. The available census and Head Start data records whether people speak a language other than English, so these figures assume that an educator in the state of Massachusetts most likely speaks English.

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total number of childcare workers and pre-k and kindergarten teachers that speak a language other than English in MA (estimate)"

teacher_lang_summary <- ma_pums_recoded |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  filter(LANX == 1) |>
  summarize(prop = n() / 623)

teacher_summary <- ma_pums_recoded |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  summarize(prop = n() / 74617)

total_teacher_est <- total_pop_ma$estimate[[1]] * teacher_summary$prop

total_bilingual_teacher_est <- total_teacher_est * teacher_lang_summary$prop * 100

list(
  icon = "hash",
  color = "info",
  value = round(total_bilingual_teacher_est )
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Proportion of childcare workers and pre-k and kindergarten teachers that speak a language other than English in MA"

teacher_lang_percent <- teacher_lang_summary$prop * 100

list(
  icon = "percent",
  color = "info",
  value = round(teacher_lang_percent, 2)
)
```

## Temporal Visualizations
```{r}
#| fill: false

#note: make this into a function to do other states
earlyed_2024 <- pums_recoded_2024 |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  mutate(year = 2024)
earlyed_2023 <- pums_recoded_2023 |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  mutate(year = 2023)
earlyed_2022 <- pums_recoded_2022 |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  mutate(year = 2022) |>
  rename(STATE = ST,
         STATE_label = ST_label)
earlyed_2021 <- pums_recoded_2021 |>
  filter(OCCP == 2300 | OCCP == 4600) |>
  mutate(year = 2021) |>
  rename(STATE = ST,
         STATE_label = ST_label)

# add column for year, join together, split into ma vs everywhere else, visualize

combined_earlyed <- dplyr::bind_rows(earlyed_2024, earlyed_2023, earlyed_2022, earlyed_2021)

combined_earlyed |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(STATE == 25 ~ "MA",
                           STATE != 25 ~ "Other States")) |>
  group_by(year, is_ma) |>
  filter(!is.na(is_ma)) |>
  summarize(total_earlyeds = n(),
            total_bilingual = sum(LANX == 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           is_ma != "MA" ~ "USA"),
         total_earlyeds = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ total_earlyeds,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(total_earlyeds, na.rm = TRUE)),
         total_bilingual = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ total_bilingual,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(total_bilingual)),
          percent_bilingual = total_bilingual / total_earlyeds * 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = percent_bilingual, col = is_ma, group = is_ma)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = min(year):max(year)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hs_palette) +
  labs(x = "Year",
       y = "Percent of Multilingual Early Educators", 
       title = "MA Has A Higher Proportion of Multilingual Early Educators, But That's Decreasing",
       subtitle = "American Community Survey Public Use Microdata Sample, 2021-2024") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| fill: false

#get pop of ma vs US for all years, multiply by percent early ed, multiply by percent bilingual, divide hs number by that number


bilingual_ma_vs_usa <- combined_earlyed |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(STATE == 25 ~ "MA",
                           STATE != 25 ~ "Other States")) |>
  group_by(year, is_ma) |>
  filter(!is.na(is_ma)) |>
  summarize(total_earlyeds = n(),
            total_bilingual = sum(LANX == 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           is_ma != "MA" ~ "USA"),
         total_earlyeds = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ total_earlyeds,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(total_earlyeds, na.rm = TRUE)),
         total_bilingual = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ total_bilingual,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(total_bilingual)),
          percent_bilingual = total_bilingual / total_earlyeds * 100)

ma_vs_usa_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(total_pop_by_year, total_pop_ma_acs1)

ma_vs_usa_pop <- ma_vs_usa_pop |>
  mutate(year = case_when(year == 1 ~ 2021,
                          year == 2 ~ 2022,
                          year == 3 ~ 2023,
                          year == 4 ~ 2024),
         is_ma = case_when(GEOID == 1 ~ "USA",
                           GEOID == 25 ~ "MA"))

bilingual_vs_total <- left_join(ma_vs_usa_pop, bilingual_ma_vs_usa)

earlyeds_prop_usa_2021 <- nrow(earlyed_2021)/nrow(pums_recoded_2021) 
earlyeds_prop_usa_2022 <- nrow(earlyed_2022)/nrow(pums_recoded_2022)
earlyeds_prop_usa_2023 <- nrow(earlyed_2023)/nrow(pums_recoded_2023)
earlyeds_prop_usa_2024 <- nrow(earlyed_2021)/nrow(pums_recoded_2024)
earlyeds_prop_ma_2021 <- nrow(earlyed_2021["STATE" == 25])/nrow(pums_recoded_2021["ST" = 25])
earlyeds_prop_ma_2022 <- nrow(earlyed_2022["STATE" == 25])/nrow(pums_recoded_2022["ST" = 25])
earlyeds_prop_ma_2023 <- nrow(earlyed_2023["STATE" == 25])/nrow(pums_recoded_2023["STATE" = 25])
earlyeds_prop_ma_2024 <- nrow(earlyed_2024["STATE" == 25])/nrow(pums_recoded_2024["STATE" = 25])
prop_earlyed <- c(earlyeds_prop_usa_2021, earlyeds_prop_usa_2022, earlyeds_prop_usa_2023, earlyeds_prop_usa_2024, earlyeds_prop_ma_2021, earlyeds_prop_ma_2023, earlyeds_prop_ma_2022, earlyeds_prop_ma_2021)

bilingual_vs_total$prop_earlyed <- prop_earlyed

bilingual_vs_total <- bilingual_vs_total |>
  mutate(est_total_bilingual_earlyed = estimate * prop_earlyed * percent_bilingual / 100)

hs <- pir_b |>
  filter(pir_year != 2025) |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(State == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           State != "MA" ~ "Other States")) |>
  group_by(pir_year, is_ma) |>
  filter(!is.na(is_ma)) |>
  summarize(bilingual_teachers_etc = sum(B.14, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
              ungroup() |>
  group_by(pir_year) |>
  mutate(is_ma = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ "MA",
                           is_ma != "MA" ~ "USA"),
         bilingual_teachers_etc = case_when(is_ma == "MA" ~ bilingual_teachers_etc,
                           is_ma == "USA" ~ sum(bilingual_teachers_etc, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  rename(year = pir_year)

bilingual_vs_total <- left_join(bilingual_vs_total, hs)
bilingual_vs_total <- bilingual_vs_total |>
  mutate(percent_served = bilingual_teachers_etc / est_total_bilingual_earlyed * 100)

bilingual_vs_total |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = percent_served, col = is_ma, group = is_ma)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = min(year):max(year)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hs_palette) +
  labs(x = "Year",
       y = "Percent of Bilingual Early Educators Working At HS*", 
       title = "Percent of Bilingual Early Educators Working at Head Start, 2021-2024*",
       subtitle = "American Community Survey, American Community Survey Public Use Microdata Sample, Head Start Program Information Report, 2021-2025") +
  theme_minimal()
```
